source.title: A Case Study of How Intuition and Reasoning Interact in Language Models
source.authors: Simon Henniger; Arnau Marin-Llobet; Rhea E Karty; Nada Amin

record.tranche_reason: Tests a refusal direction and additional harmfulness and scrutiny directions in a reasoning model. The reported refusal-vector effects are brittle and can cause no-final collapse; the authors argue refusal in this model is an interaction among multiple components.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the original single-refusal-direction study, but cited results are not included as findings. Direction-selection values are recorded only where they measure separation or geometry; vector-choice and hyperparameter-selection details alone are omitted.
record.test_reason: Computes a difference-in-means harmful-vs-harmless refusal direction (read at the last chain-of-thought token) in the reasoning model GPT-OSS-120B. It steers along this direction to remove and induce refusal, and argues refusal in this model is not a single linear feature. This bears on V8, on V1 in a reasoning model, and on V5 through a separate harmfulness direction.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that refusal in GPT-OSS-120B is the interaction of an intuitive harmfulness signal, explicit CoT reasoning, and a scrutiny coupling mechanism, rather than a single linear feature. They report refusal-vector steering flips behavior only in a narrow window before no-final collapse. Scrutiny steering plus a harmless CoT prefill overrides refusal on all 65 harmful prompts. On AgentHarm, refusal steering with prefill scores highest (0.346), with scrutiny plus prefill (0.337) close behind; both need the prefill.
record.recipe_differences: The study computes harmful-versus-harmless difference-in-means directions, but its refusal vector is measured at the last token of the chain of thought and steered at selected layers during generation. It does not ablate one direction at every layer and position; it also studies scrutiny and harmfulness vectors.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on the vector family, steering strength α, prompt category (robust versus manipulable), and whether a CoT is prefilled. Scrutiny steering has no compliance effect on robust harmful prompts without a prefill; strong refusal-vector steering leads to no-final collapse.

fits_no_version.finding: A scrutiny direction (mismatched vs matched prompt/CoT pairs, d=3.87, layers 20–22) gates whether CoT reasoning controls the answer. Alone it has no effect on robust harmful prompts (0/30). Combined with a harmless CoT prefill it yields compliance on all 65 harmful prompts and AgentHarm score 0.337.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In deliberatively aligned reasoning models, a prompt/CoT coherence direction gates whether the chain-of-thought conclusion overrides the intuitive harmfulness signal in the refusal decision.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering along the prompt-harmfulness direction raises compliance on manipulable harmful prompts from 0% to 69% at α=−3, but collapses AgentHarm performance (0 tool calls).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A pre-deliberative harmfulness direction, partly aligned with the refusal readout, causally shifts refusal in reasoning models at a capability cost.

record.peer_reviewed: ICML 2026 Workshop on Mechanistic Interpretability; PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The core evidence is a case study on one model and 142 prompts. The refusal-vector intervention is steering rather than full-layer, full-position ablation. The authors note that the adapted AgentHarm results are not directly comparable to the original benchmark and that only 44% of cases complete all required tool calls at the best operating point.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the many per-α, per-vector-family and per-prompt-category steering-table cells in Appendix G beyond the summarized refusal-vector and scrutiny results. Also omitted additional AgentHarm category-level rows and scrutiny α settings; the selected rows capture the reported outcomes relevant to the claim versions.

untested.parts: Directional ablation at all layers and positions was not done; only activation addition/subtraction at top-1 or top-3 layers. General capability benchmarks were not run beyond AgentHarm and C/R/NF classification.
No jailbreak analysis and no adversarial training.
No affine, cone or multi-dimensional subspace test of refusal itself. The authors argue for multiple components, but the extra directions encode other contrasts (coherence, prompt harmfulness).
No cross-language, cross-variant or base-to-instruct transfer.
Only one reasoning model, GPT-OSS-120B; no other reasoning models compared.

missing.what: Refusal-direction subtraction without CoT prefill. Robust harmful no-prefill goes 0/0/30 at α=0, to 24/0/6 at −1, to 30/0/0 at −1.25 to −2, to 0/30/0 at −3. Manipulable harmful reaches 35/0/0 at −1.25. Harmless prompts still comply at these α. This is the cleanest V1/V8 removal test, and it seems at odds with the text's claim that single-vector no-prefill steering reaches 'far lower' compliance.

Refusal-direction addition without prefill on harmless prompts. Robust safe goes 30/0/0, to 8/17/5 at α=1, to 0/21/9 at α=1.5. Manipulable safe goes to 0/23/24 at α=1.5. Refusal is induced only alongside heavy no-final collapse.
Coherence-judge thresholds (grey regions, Llama 3.3 70B) for refusal-vector α values, needed to tell whether the comply outputs at α −1.25 to −2 are coherent.

record.verdict_notes: The refusal 'direction' here is read at the last CoT token and applied by additive steering at chosen layers, not ablation, so it is only a close analogue of the original. The paper's claim of brittleness rests mostly on collapse at large |α| and on coherence judgments. The full Table 27 counts show complete removal of refusal across a range of α, so 'challenges' was downgraded to limits_scope. The record's V4 'supports' label was dropped: non-collinear directions built from different contrasts (coherence, prompt content) do not show that refusal itself is multi-dimensional. The harmful vector's causal effect on compliance (R11) is suggestive but confounded by its 0.54 cosine with the refusal direction. Single model, 142 prompts.

versions.untested_parts: Tests steering of a harmful-versus-harmless difference-in-means refusal vector in one reasoning model, not projecting the vector out of every layer and position. The vector is measured at the end of the chain of thought and injected at selected layer(s) during generated tokens; adding it is not reported as the exact all-layer/all-position intervention in the claim.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration experiment.
No jailbreak attack designed to suppress the refusal direction and no training against its ablation.
Tests whether distinct directions and interacting mechanisms matter; it does not test affine or cone formulations specifically.
The harmful vector contrasts harmful and harmless prompts as a proxy for harmfulness; the paper does not directly evaluate a separate harmfulness-judgment output.
No language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
Vector training-set variants are tested, but refusal-training interventions or when refusal is trained are not.
Tests one reasoning model, GPT-OSS-120B; no broader comparison across reasoning models.
